title: Bodycam Footage Of Phoenix Police Shooting Man With Machete
description:
* (Disclaimer: This video content is intended for educational and informational purposes only) *
Phoenix, Arizona — The Phoenix Police department released body-camera footage of an officer involved shooting that occurred on May 1, 2022, just after 12:00 p.m., in the roadway to the south of 19th Avenue and Southern Avenue. Officers from the South Mountain Precinct were in the parking lot of a gas station near 19th Avenue and Southern Avenue working through an unrelated matter when they were notified of a man with a machete in an open field to the south. Officers contacted the man and gave him commands to drop the machete as he walked eastbound in the field towards 19th Avenue. Officers continued to order the man to drop the machete while following him as he walked southbound in the roadway of 19th Avenue. The man was shouting in Spanish. Due to the language barrier, officers were unable to understand what he was saying. 

There were vehicles driving by on 19th Avenue and pedestrians walking on the nearby sidewalks. While the man was in the middle lane of 19th Avenue, an officer with a stunbag shotgun approached him and gave repeated commands to drop the machete. The officer delivered several rounds from the stunbag which did not seem to affect the man. He continued to yell in Spanish while advancing towards the officer with the machete still in hand. The officer transitioned to his handgun and fired, striking the man and ending the threat. Officers approached the man, removed the machete, and began rendering first aid. Officers continued until Phoenix Fire responded and assumed care. The man was transported to a local hospital in critical condition where he remains hospitalized but will later be booked into jail on one count of aggravated assault on a police officer once his condition improves. There were no injuries to other community members or officers.

An officer was at a gas station in the area working through an unrelated call for service when he was notified by a community member about a man nearby who was waving a machete. The officer saw the adult male suspect walking south along 19th Avenue on the sidewalk, waving the machete around, before eventually walking into a vacant dirt lot. The officer called for backup and they tried to keep the suspect contained to the dirt lot away from other community members. Negative separate issue. He's threatened a couple patrons of the key of T, but right now it seems like a 918 issue, but he's got a machete in his hand. He's threatening passing cars. I don't know how many calls you're gonna get on this. I might move my car over there in case he goes that way. Keep him off the street. Like put my car over there, keep him from going to the street. You stay that way. Put it down. Put it down. Put it down. Drop it. I'll let him. We're going to need a knife. The suspect ignored the officer and continued walking southbound along 19th Avenue and eventually into the roadway. The third officer to arrive retrieved a less lethal stun bag shotgun from his patrol vehicle before approaching the suspect. A knife, bro. You're going to get stun bags. Drop the knife, bro, right now. Drop the knife. Drop the knife. Drop the knife. Get back. Drop the fucking knife. Drop the fucking... Drop the knife! Here's a portion of the body warrant camera video from the fourth officer on scene who positioned his vehicle in the roadway to the south of the suspect. Here is another look at the same video, digitally stabilized. The suspect dropped the machete on the ground and officers were able to move it away as they approached him to take him into the to custody and begin first aid. The officers continued to provide first aid until the Phoenix Fire Department arrived and assumed care before transporting the suspect to a local hospital for treatment. No other community members or officers were injured during this incident.
